memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'You must obey my laws and be careful to follow my decrees. I am the LORD your God. Keep my decrees and laws, for the person who obeys them will live by them. I am the LORD.'" - Lev 18:4-5 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The person who obeys them will live by them. God's commands are not designed to diminish life but to sustain it.

We rarely feel that. Rules feel like restriction — fences keeping us from what we want. And Scripture is honest that obedience often costs something.

But consider how the world actually works. A river without banks is not a freer river; it is a swamp. Music without structure is not liberated; it is noise. The constraints are what make the thing possible.

Jesus said it directly: I have come that they may have life, and have it to the full (John 10:10). He was not offering a narrower existence. He was offering a fuller one.

We should also hear the ache in this verse. Paul quotes it in Galatians precisely to show that no one has ever managed it. The person who obeys will live — but nobody has fully obeyed. That is why he writes: Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law by becoming a curse for us (Gal 3:13).

So this verse cuts two ways. God's commands genuinely lead to life. And our failure to keep them is exactly why we need a Saviour who kept them for us.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you experience God's commands as restriction or as protection?
2. Where has obedience actually produced more life for you, not less?
3. What does it mean that Christ kept the law perfectly in your place?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that Your commands are for my flourishing and not against it. Where I have failed to keep them, thank You that Christ kept them for me. Amen.
